# Do LLMs Understand Ambiguity in Text?

> A study of 1,000 ambiguous open-domain questions (AmbigQA, from Google's NQ-Open) with GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini. Off-the-shelf LLMs pick one reading of an ambiguous question and answer it confidently; simple, training-free, token-level disambiguation prompts — rephrasing with "what", or adding model-generated context — measurably improve ground-truth answer overlap, with adding context best. Published at IEEE BigData 2024 (DOI 10.1109/BigData62323.2024.10825265).

Paper: "Do LLMs Understand Ambiguity in Text? A Case Study in Open-world Question Answering" by Aryan Keluskar, Amrita Bhattacharjee, and Huan Liu (School of Computing & AI, Arizona State University). Published at the 2024 IEEE International Conference on Big Data (IEEE BigData), pages 7485–7490.

## Key facts

- Task: open-domain QA over 1,000 ambiguous questions sampled from AmbigQA (a subset of Google's NQ-Open); answers scored by cosine similarity of OpenAI text-embedding-3-large embeddings against ground truth ("GT answer overlap", higher is better).
- Models: GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini.
- Baselines: naive prompting; few-shot fine-tuning (50 ambiguous QA pairs); temperature ablation.
- Rephrasing a question to begin with "what" makes it more specific and raises GT answer overlap (GPT-4o 0.759 → 0.778).
- Adding context generated from the model's own world knowledge works best (GPT-4o 0.759 → 0.789; GPT-4o-mini 0.692 → 0.71), and tracks the human-disambiguated upper bound (0.858 / 0.783).
- Small-scale fine-tuning did not help: GPT-4o-mini slightly degraded (0.626 vs. 0.643 naive), likely from catastrophic forgetting.
- Lowering temperature from 1.0 to 0.2 produced only minor, non-significant changes.
- Ambiguity matters for fact-checking, question answering, feature extraction, and sentiment analysis: models misinterpret ambiguous input, hallucinate, and answer the wrong question confidently.
